digest.lead: Claude Code v2.1.158 brings Auto mode to enterprise cloud platforms, while a mystery company's $500M spending mishap highlights the need for better usage controls.
digest.summary: Today also saw plugin management improvements in Claude Code and community discussion around AI engineering roles.

stories.headline: Mystery Company Burns $500M on Claude in Single Month Due to Missing Usage Limits
stories.summary: An unidentified company accidentally spent $500 million on Claude AI services in one month after failing to implement usage limits on employee licenses [3]. The incident highlights critical gaps in enterprise cost management for AI services.
key_points: Company lacked proper usage controls on Claude licenses
Massive overspend occurred within a single billing period
stories.impact: This serves as a wake-up call for enterprises deploying Claude at scale, emphasizing the urgent need for robust usage monitoring and spending controls in AI procurement strategies.

sources.title: Mystery company accidentally blew $500M on Claude AI in a single month

stories.headline: Claude Code Auto Mode Expands to Enterprise Cloud Platforms
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.158 brings Auto mode support to Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry for Opus 4.7 and 4.8 models [1]. Users can enable the feature by setting the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 environment variable.
stories.impact: Enterprise developers using cloud-hosted Claude instances can now access autonomous coding capabilities, potentially accelerating development workflows in corporate environments.

stories.headline: Claude Code Streamlines Plugin Development with Local Directory Support
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.157 introduces automatic loading of plugins from `.claude/skills` directories and adds `claude plugin init <name>` for scaffolding new plugins [2]. The update also enhances autocomplete for plugin commands and improves agent session management.
key_points: No marketplace required for local plugin development
Enhanced autocomplete for plugin commands and names
Agent settings now persist across dispatched sessions
stories.impact: These changes lower the barrier for custom plugin development and improve the developer experience for teams building specialized Claude Code workflows.

stories.headline: Community Discusses AI Engineering Role Definition
stories.summary: A Hacker News discussion explores the evolving definition of "AI Engineer" roles, generating 29 comments from practitioners sharing their perspectives on skills and responsibilities [5].
stories.impact: This ongoing conversation reflects the industry's struggle to define emerging AI-focused roles as Claude and other AI tools reshape software development practices.

sources.title: Ask HN: What Is an "AI Engineer"?

stories.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values

stories.headline: Use `/team-onboarding` command to generate teammate ramp-up guides
stories.summary: Claude Code can automatically create onboarding documentation for new team members based on your local usage patterns. This saves time creating training materials and ensures consistency in how team members learn your workflows.
actionable_steps: Update to Claude Code v2.1.101 or later
Run the `/team-onboarding` command in your Claude Code interface
Review the generated ramp-up guide and customize as needed
Share the guide with new team members

stories.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
stories.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

stories.headline: Use `/tui fullscreen` for flicker-free Claude Code rendering
stories.summary: The `/tui fullscreen` command switches Claude Code to a flicker-free rendering mode within the same conversation. This improves visual stability and reduces screen flicker during interactions.
actionable_steps: Press Enter to activate flicker-free rendering mode

stories.headline: Use the path parameter with EnterWorktree to switch between git worktrees
stories.summary: The EnterWorktree tool now accepts a path parameter that lets you switch into existing worktrees of your current repository. This makes it easier to work with multiple branches or feature development in parallel without switching repositories.
actionable_steps: Identify the worktree path you want to switch to in your current repository
Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter: `EnterWorktree(path="/path/to/your/worktree")`
Verify you're in the correct worktree by checking the current branch or directory
